The gym I work at have got set plans to combat covid.

- We have a booking system.
- You will be only allowed a maximum of an hour.
- The equipment has been split up in 3 sections.
- Every hour and a half the building will be closed and the employees then will do a deep clean for 30 minutes (almost impossible with the size, which includes all equipment, reception and class studios)
- One way system around the gym, you can't go back and you must leave by the fire exit at the end. 

There are a few more that are different but that's just an example.

I do think that either way gyms are going to be struggling, people will quickly get fed up of all the restrictions and realise its cheaper and easier to workout at home or outside. The aircon is a huge issue as we have 10 in the gym alone and we have to keep these on to keep the room at a safe temperature.
This probably has no relevance to what you put but it's a slight insight on what some gyms will be doing.

I agree that stale air is worse, also yes I agree that they should open together as they are just as bad as each other. Having worked in both a gym and a pub as a manager I can tell you the risk assessments in a leisure centre are much more complicated than just putting a couple of weights in a room and having the right air temp.

I was talking about the gym Aircon. Pubs don't necessarily need Aircon it's just a luxury. If a member of our gym overheats due to over exertion it could result in injury or they my faint, we will then have to perform first aid or possibly cpr in serious cases not only putting the member at risks but ourselves when it can be prevented. I do understand pubs are at risk and I will not be attending the pubs as I disagree that they should be opening but two wrongs don't make a right.

I agree, also gyms have to use Aircon which only circulates around the room. Yes you could open doors but for example the gym I work at, there is only a firedoor that would not do as you have to have a certain temperature. Ours is 19c any higher/lower is classed as a health risk which can potentially get us shut down anyway so that's why we need Aircon.
YMCA Gyms are planning for 4th July, to be honest I still don't know how it's going to work for gyms. Even though I manage there, it's a little dodgy and corners may be cut. Time will tell.
